title: Rainbow trapezoids with given area
summary: A well-known result by Graham in Euclidean Ramsey Theory states that, for every positive real number $A$, every coloring of the plane with finite number of colors contains a monochromatic triangle of area $A$. We consider canonical versions of this result. We show that every $3$-coloring of the plane integer lattice contains either a rainbow triangle of area $1/2$ or a monochromatic rectangle of any given area whose sides are parallell to the axes.
